full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J:-  At the instance of the plaintiff this appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.04.1995 passed by a Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 842 of 1990, under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act, making the Rule absolute and consequent thereupon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 14.04.90 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court and S.C.C. Judge, Tangail in S.C.C. Suit No. 2 of 1992, decreeing the Suit for ejectment of monthly tenant. 

 5. Upon hearing the parties, the trial court decreed the suit. Defendant then took the revision before the High Court Division. The High Court Division on contest made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court finding inter alia that the plaintiff could not prove that the defendant was a defaulter and it was doubtful that the plaintiff bonafide required the suit premises bonafide for rebuilding and thus dismissed the suit. 

 7. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff appellant submits that the plaintiff could prove that the defendant did not pay any rent from 1388 B.S. and before that also rent was not paid regularly and this evidence could not be dislodged or disproved by the defendant. It is clear that even if according to the deed of agreement creating tenancy Tk. 25/- only would be adjusted towards the monthly rent for every month from the said deposited money, which is said to be the security money still the balance amount of the rent should have been paid by the tenant defendant. But the defendant having not paid any rent from 1388 B.S. It is undeniably proved that the defendant is a defaulter. Mr. Islam also submits that so far the bonafide requirement for personal use and occupation of the suit premises after rebuilding is concerned, it is amply proved by the plaintiff vide Ext. 5 series that the plan was obtained by the plaintiff from the local Pourshava authority which was approved by the Sub-divisional Officer and was passed by the Chairman of the Pourshava who were the admitted legal authority for the purpose and as such the plaintiff also could prove bonafide requirement of the premises for the purpose rebuilding. Mr. Mahmudul Islam submits that on both these counts that is on the question of default in payment of monthly rent and bonafide requirement the High Court Division misconceived the law and fact in making the Rule absolute and in setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court who decreed the suit. 

 15. For the reasons and discussions made above, we find merits in this appeal. Accordingly the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside and the suit for ejectment is decreed.
